bib.title: AgentFold: Long-Horizon Web Agents with Proactive Context Management

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "AgentFold: Long-Horizon Web Agents with Proactive Context Management", Rui Ye, Zhongwang Zhang, Kuan Li, Huifeng Yin et al. (Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group), arXiv:2510.24699v1 [cs.CL], 28 Oct 2025 (dated 2025-10-29). Preprint, not peer reviewed.

COVERAGE: Read the whole extraction (91,790 chars), all pages. Main text through the Conclusions, Table 1 and the references, then the appendix. The appendix (A.1 case studies, Tables 2-3, Figures 6-9, about chars 54k-91k) is context-trace tables and example prompts and responses with no new results. I skimmed it. Figure captions came from the figures script. The PDF text holds no embedded instructions.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Folding keeps context small. Average context grows from about 3.5k to 7k tokens over 100 turns.
  number: 3.5k to 7k tokens
  setup: AgentFold-30B-A3B, 200 BrowseComp trajectories, 100-turn cap, 128k model context.
  quote: "The average token count grows at a remarkably slow, sub-linear rate, less than doubling from approximately 3.5k to 7k over 100 turns"
  where: p.8-9, Fig 3a

- At turn 100 the AgentFold context is far smaller than a ReAct context. The ReAct context length is read off the Figure 1 plot, not a separate experiment.
  number: over 84k tokens (92%) smaller, about 7GB memory saving per inference instance
  setup: same BrowseComp trajectories, compared with a standard ReAct baseline at turn 100.
  quote: "AgentFold’s context is, on average, over84k tokens (92%) smallerthan ReAct’s. This token reduction also has profound implications for computational resource requirements, translating to an estimated memory saving of nearly7GB per inference instance"
  where: p.9

- Headline benchmark scores for the SFT-only 30B model (3B active). The paper gives no ablation of folding against no folding.
  number: BrowseComp 36.2, BrowseComp-ZH 47.3, WideSearch 62.1 (Item-F1), GAIA 67.0 (text-only)
  setup: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 fine-tuned with SFT only, 100 tool-call cap. Benchmarks with fewer than 200 samples are averaged over 3 trials.
  quote: "AgentFold-30B-A3B (Ours) 36.2 47.3 62.1 67.0"
  where: Table 1, p.8
  Comparisons from the same table: DeepSeek-V3.1-671B 30.0 / 49.2 / - / 63.1; GLM-4.5-355B 26.4 / 37.5 / - / 66.0; o4-mini 28.3 / 44.3; o3 49.7 / 58.1 / 60.0 / 70.5; OpenAI Deep Research 51.5 / 42.9 / - / 67.4; Claude-4-Sonnet 14.7 / 22.5 / 62.0 / 68.3. It beats DeepSeek on BrowseComp but loses to it on BrowseComp-ZH. It trails o3 and Deep Research on BrowseComp. Some baseline numbers were "taken from corresponding papers or leaderboards".

- With more turns, AgentFold keeps improving while the GLM-4.5 agent plateaus.
  number: turn limits 8 to 256, the exact accuracies are only in the Fig 4 plot
  setup: BrowseComp, AgentFold-30B-A3B against GLM-4.5-355B-A32B.
  quote: "our smaller model consistently outperforms the 355B baseline at all comparable turn limits. (2) Second, the GLM-4.5 agent’s performance saturates and fails as its append-only context fills, while AgentFold’s accuracy continues to improve steadily up to 256 turns"
  where: p.10

- In a 500-turn run the context mostly stays under 20k tokens and does not grow monotonically. The authors credit deep consolidation of failed sub-trajectories, but this is not tested directly.
  number: 500 turns, below 20k tokens
  setup: extended BrowseComp experiment, shown in Figure 1. No accuracy given.
  quote: "increasing the maximum number of turns to 500, with the context length dynamics reported in Figure 1. The results reveal that the context mostly remains below 20k tokens and, notably, does not grow monotonically."
  where: p.10

- Over 20% of tasks hit the 100-turn limit and count as failures. At that point the context is only about 7k tokens, so the cap is the bottleneck rather than context space.
  number: over 20%, about 7k tokens of 128k
  setup: 200 BrowseComp trajectories.
  quote: "over 20% of tasks being forcibly terminated at our experimental limit of 100 turns, which are typically marked as failure. Crucially, at this termination point, the agent’s context is only ≈7k tokens"
  where: p.8-9

- Block count grows sub-linearly under AgentFold and linearly under ReAct. A block is one summary entry plus the latest interaction.
  number: none (plot only, Fig 3b)
  quote: "In stark contrast to the linear explosion of ReAct, AgentFold’s block count grows at a slow, sub-linear rate."
  where: p.9

- Repeated full-history summarization compounds detail loss. This is an illustrative calculation with an assumed 1% loss per re-summarization, not a measurement.
  number: 36.6% survival at step 100; 0.66% at step 500
  quote: "if we assume a modest 1% chance of a key detail being lost each time the full history is re-summarized,the probability of a finding from step 1 surviving until step 100 reduces to just ≈36.6%(0.99 100)... after 500 steps... only0.66%( 0.99500)"
  where: p.7, Section 3.5

- Design: the context is C_t = (Q, T, S_{t-2}, I_{t-1}). That is the question, the tools, multi-scale state summaries (older steps, folded) and the latest interaction (kept verbatim). Each step the model outputs thinking, a folding directive, an explanation and a tool call. The folding directive is JSON {"range":[k,t-1],"summary":...}.
  - k = t-1 is granular condensation: one step becomes one summary.
  - k < t-1 is deep consolidation: the latest interaction and prior summaries become one coarse block.
  number: none
  quote: "Granular Condensation( k=t− 1): This operation folds only theLatest Interactioninto a new, fine-grained summary." and "Deep Consolidation( k<t− 1): This operation performs a change of scale by fusing theLatest Interactionwith a chain of prior summaries into a single, coarse-grained summary."
  where: p.5-6, Section 3.3

- Training: the Fold-Generator pipeline builds trajectories from the WebSailor question set. Prompting alone cannot reliably produce the structured output. Rejection sampling drops steps that break the format and trajectories with too many environment errors. Plain SFT then trains the model. No continual pre-training and no RL.
  number: none
  quote: "even the most advanced LLMs cannot reliably produce AgentFold’s accurate, structured, multi-part responses through prompt engineering alone"
  where: p.6, Section 3.4

- Case study: after 11 failed steps (6-16) the agent folds them into one conclusion and pivots to new queries.
  number: steps 6-16
  quote: "it performs aDeep Consolidation, folding the entire 11-step failed sequence into a single, conclusive summary."
  where: p.10-11, Fig 5

LIMITS
- No ablation isolates folding from SFT data quality or the base model. No head-to-head against full-history-summarization baselines such as MEM1 or MemAgent. Those are only argued against, and the authors note they were evaluated on simpler HotpotQA-style tasks.
- The ReAct baseline for token and memory comparisons is only plotted in Figure 1, with no table.
- No latency, cost or fold-error analysis. Nothing measures how often a fold drops a needed detail, and folds are irreversible, as the authors' own criticism of summarization implies.
- Authors concede: only plain SFT, "without extensive optimization". RL for folding policies is left to future work. Scaling beyond 256 turns is "deferred to future work due to time constraints".
- The 100-turn cap penalises all tasks. 500-turn accuracy is not reported.
- Several baseline numbers are copied from papers and leaderboards, so the settings are not necessarily matched. Single run on large benchmarks, 3 trials on small ones, no variance given.
- The 7GB saving is "estimated".

BUILDS ON: ReAct (Yao et al., 2023); MEM1 (Zhou et al., 2025b) and MemAgent (Yu et al., 2025), the step-wise full-history summarizers it contrasts with; WebSailor (Li et al., 2025a/b) for the question set and agents; Qwen3 (Yang et al., 2025) as the base model; Miller 1956 and Newell et al. 1972 as the cognitive-science motivation; context-engineering survey (Mei et al., 2025); Mem0 (Chhikara et al., 2025), A-mem (Xu et al., 2025) and MemOS (Li et al., 2025d) for external context augmentation, which it distinguishes from its own intra-task curation.

CODE: none (no pseudocode). The folding directive format, verbatim from the Figure 5 example:
{"range": [6, 16], "summary": "..."}
The context rendering is "[Folded Step 1 to 3] …", "[Folded Step 8] …", "[Step 9] Explanation / Tool Call / Tool Response" (Fig 2, p.4).

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.1): performance plus context length against ReAct and the 500-turn run. Best single picture of the claim.
- Fig 2 (p.4): context layout, with granular condensation and deep consolidation before and after. Shows the mechanism fastest.
- Fig 3a and 3b (p.9): token and block growth curves.
- Fig 4 (p.10): BrowseComp accuracy against turn limit, AgentFold against GLM-4.5.
- Fig 5 (p.10): a worked deep-consolidation example.
- Figs 6-9 (pp.23-26): appendix case-study contexts and responses.

PROBLEMS: None serious. The text extraction is clean apart from missing spaces around italics. Figure data (Fig 1, 3, 4) is plot-only, so the exact accuracy values per turn limit are not in the text.
